about.founderDesc: Ms. Snigdhaa Ritesh is a journalist with 16 years of experience in electronic and print media. Through her work, she has closely witnessed the challenges that women face in society. Her passion for creating a safer, more aware and empowered community of women led to the inception of Pink Shakti.

items.h112Desc: India all-in-one emergency helpline number 112 was launched by Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh in 16 states and Union Territories. The 112 emergency helpline number would provide immediate assistance for any kind of emergency services for citizens like police help, hospital emergency, fire case women safety issue and child protection. Any citizen in distress situation can dial 112 and immediate help will reach to him or her within minutes.
items.h181Desc: 181 is a National Helpline in India that serves as a dedicated support system for women facing adversity. With a focus on issues like domestic violence and harassment, it offers a safe space for women to seek help. Beyond immediate aid, Helpline 181 provides counselling, legal assistance, and rescue services, contributing significantly to women safety and well-being across the country.
items.h1090Desc: Women Power Line 1090 in Uttar Pradesh is a proactive initiative combating crimes against women. This helpline offers a rapid response to reports of harassment, stalking, and abuse, reinforcing women safety. By empowering women to speak out and seek assistance, Women Power Line 1090 plays a crucial role in building a secure and supportive community for women in the region.

purpose.title: Purpose and Objective
purpose.desc: The Prevention of Sexual Harassment (PoSH) Act, 2013 aims to protect women against sexual harassment at the workplace and to provide a safe and secure working environment. It also provides a mechanism for filing and redressing complaints.

definition.title: Definition of Sexual Harassment
definition.intro: As per the Act, sexual harassment includes any one or more of the following (whether directly or by implication):
bullets: Demand or request for sexual favors.
Any other unwelcome physical, verbal or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.

scope.title: Scope of the Act
bullets: Any place visited by a woman in the course of her employment, including transportation.

icc.title: Internal Complaints Committee (ICC)
icc.desc: Every employer with 10 or more employees is required to constitute an Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) at each office or branch. The ICC must have a Presiding Officer who is a senior woman employee and at least two other members who are committed to the cause of women or have experience in social work, legal knowledge or experience in dealing with sexual harassment issues.

shebox.title: SHe-Box
shebox.desc: SHe-Box is an online complaint management platform launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development (Government of India) for lodging complaints of sexual harassment at the workplace.
shebox.stepsHeading: Steps to File a Complaint on SHe-Box
steps: Enter details of complainant, workplace and respondent.
Describe the complaint and upload supporting documents (if any).
Submit the complaint and note the reference number to track the status.

bnsSection79Page.subtitle: Outraging the Modesty of Women / Eve Teasing
bnsSection79Page.desc: Know about the legal provisions, punishments and your rights to stay safe, aware and empowered.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.desc: BNS Section 79 covers words, gestures or any act intended to outrage the modesty of a woman. This includes any behaviour that is indecent, obscene or unwelcome and makes a woman feel uncomfortable, humiliated or unsafe in a public or private place.

constituents.title: Main Constituents
bullets: Obscene words or gestures directed towards a woman.
Any act intended to outrage the modesty of a woman.
Can be committed in public or private place, including online through messages, calls or social media.

punishment.title: Punishment
punishment.line1: Imprisonment for a term which may extend up to 3 years and/or fine as per law.
punishment.line2: Punishment may vary based on the circumstances of the case.

examples.title: Examples of Such Offences
bullets: Eve teasing in public places like streets, markets, schools or colleges.
Sending inappropriate messages or images online.
Any behaviour that humiliates or makes a woman feel unsafe.

equalPayPage.desc: Women have the right to receive equal pay for equal work without discrimination.

explanation.title: Explanation
explanation.desc: Every woman has the right to receive equal pay for equal work. This means that a woman cannot be paid less than a man for the same work or work of a similar nature. Discrimination in wages on the basis of gender is not allowed.

constituents.title: Main Constituents
bullets: Equal pay for same work or work of similar nature.
No discrimination in wages on the basis of gender.
Equal opportunities for employment and promotion.
Women should be treated at par with men in all aspects of employment.

whatYouCanDo.title: What You Can Do
bullets: Be aware of your right to equal pay.
Speak up if you are paid less than a man for the same work.
Keep records of your work, salary and related documents.
Report discrimination to the concerned authorities or labour department.

equalPayPage.importantNoteDesc: This information is for awareness only. Laws and provisions may change over time. For current and detailed legal advice, please consult a qualified lawyer or refer to official government sources.

blogs.pageSubtitle: A Comprehensive Guide to Modern Safety
blogs.pageDesc: Insightful perspectives, actionable safety strategies, and legal knowledge to empower women across Uttar Pradesh and beyond.
blogs.titleSuffix: A Guide to Ensuring Safety in Today's World
blogs.introP1: In a world where empowerment and equality are at the forefront of discussions, ensuring women's safety remains a critical aspect of achieving true progress. Every woman deserves to feel safe and secure in her daily life, whether she's walking down the street, working late at the office, or socializing with friends.
blogs.introP2: However, the reality is that women still face numerous challenges and threats to their safety. From street harassment to domestic violence, the spectrum of dangers women encounter is vast and often daunting. But fear not, because there are concrete, proactive steps every woman can take to enhance her personal safety, reclaim her sense of security, and empower those around her.
blogs.conclusionHeading: Safety is a Collective Right, Not a Privilege.
blogs.conclusionP: In conclusion, women's safety is a collective responsibility that requires proactive measures from individuals, communities, and society as a whole. By equipping ourselves with knowledge, skills, and support networks, we can create a world where every woman feels safe, respected, and empowered to live her life to the fullest. Together, we can make safety a reality for all women.
